_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::heat#4 — NUMDOF declares how long ONOFF/VAL/FUNCT are and is checked against THEM, not against the number of transported scalars. On a 3-D HEX8 heat deck with DESIGN SURF DIRICH CONDITIONS, NUMDOF 1 with one-entry arrays and NUMDOF 2 with two-entry arrays (second VAL deliberately 7.0) both run and return the identical nodal value 5.95821728320196309e-01; the over-declared deck emits exactly one 'PROC 0 ERROR in' line, which is the deliberate recording result test (NUMDOF2_ERROR_LINES=1), so the surplus entry is dropped without comment. What IS enforced is array length == NUMDOF: NUMDOF 2 with a one-entry VAL is refused with "Failed to match condition specification in section 'DESIGN SURF DIRICH CONDITIONS'." from core/fem/src/condition/4C_fem_condition_definition.cpp, and 4C names the offending array — "Candidate parameter 'VAL' has incorrect size". Neither phrasing an earlier version of this entry quoted ('array size mismatch', 'expected NUMDOF entries') appears. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Failed to match condition specification in section 'DESIGN SURF DIRICH CONDITIONS'.

_mutation.note: make the surplus entry stop being surplus: move the odd value into the FIRST slot, which is the one the single scalar DOF actually reads. The applied boundary value changes, NUMDOF2_VALUE stops matching the NUMDOF-1 reading, and the fixture must go red — which is also what shows the comparison is sensitive to the arrays at all.
remove the pathology from the ragged arm: make the arrays the length NUMDOF declares. The condition-spec rejection and the named-array line both disappear and the fixture must go red.
